sources.note: Lists only Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List and the Strømme & Valkama 1987 survey (oai:sil.org:37718); no descriptive item.

sources.citation: Campbell, Philip J. 1991. Phonology of Pitu Ulunna Salu. In René van den Berg (ed.), Sulawesi phonologies (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 12), 1-52. Ujung Pandang: SIL. [RELATED LANGUAGE Bambam/PUS bamb1270, Salumokanam dialect -- not Dakka]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: For PUS (Bambam), sec. 3.1 p.11: stress non-phonemic, on the penultimate syllable of the word, shifting right under suffixation. Checked intro (p.3) and the 1989 thesis (sec. 1.1): coverage is the Salu Mukanam/Bambam dialect of Mambi district only; Dakka is never mentioned. Not transferable: Strømme & Valkama 1987:87 place Dakka outside the PUS Subfamily.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Barbara D. Grimes. 1987. Languages of South Sulawesi. Pacific Linguistics D-78 (Materials in Languages of Indonesia 38). Canberra: Department of Linguistics, Research School of Pacific Studies, Australian National University. viii+216 pp. doi:10.15144/PL-D78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: NOT a statement about Dakka. In the introduction to the comparative wordlists (p.94, SYMBOLS) the authors state a stock-wide default: stress in South Sulawesi languages usually falls on the penultimate syllable and is left unmarked in the lists; deviant or unclear stress is marked with an apostrophe before the stressed syllable (p.95 adds that Selayar shows some antepenultimate stress). No Tapango/Dakka wordlist was collected, so nothing in the volume bears on Dakka specifically; recorded here only because it is the field-standard source that files the Tapango-district speech inside the PUS c…

sources.citation: Nurdin, Hariadi, Awaludin, Muhammad Arif & Muhammad Hasbi. 2026. Cultural da'wah in the Mappateke Ongroang tradition of the To Dakka community in Polewali Mandar Regency. Al-Qalam (Jurnal Penelitian Agama dan Sosial Budaya) 32(1): 225-240. doi:10.31969/alq.v32i1.1898.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content: ethnography of an aqiqah-linked ritual; only an etymology of the ethnonym (To + Dakka; Taupia/Tomacoa 'good people') and two interview quotations in Dakka with Indonesian/English glosses (p.229). a full-text search for stress/accent/tekanan/aksen/fonolog/vowel/syllable: 0 hits. Reference list cites no linguistic work on Dakka.

sources.citation: Mead, David. 2014. The Dakka language. Sulawesi Language Alliance language page, sulang.org/languages/dakka (Internet Archive copy 2016-09-14).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; its bibliography for Dakka consists solely of Strømme & Valkama 1987 (plus vitality notes from Friberg & Laskowske 1989 and Wurm 2007). No grammar, phonology or wordlist materials listed.

sources.citation: Friberg, Timothy & Thomas V. Laskowske. 1989. South Sulawesi languages, 1989. In J.N. Sneddon (ed.), Studies in Sulawesi linguistics part 1 (NUSA 31), 1-17. Jakarta: Badan Penyelenggara Seri NUSA. (image scan; pp.5-6 scanned with tesseract 300 dpi)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.C.2 'Dakka' (pp.5-6): classification as South Sulawesi Stock, Northern South Sulawesi Family; 1500 speakers in Wonomulyo; children shifting to Indonesian.

sources.citation: Strømme, Kåre J. & Kari Valkama. 1987. Kabupaten Polewali Mamasa, southwestern section, and Kabupaten Majene. In Timothy Friberg (ed.), UNHAS-SIL South Sulawesi sociolinguistic surveys 1983-1987 (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 5), 59-98. Ujung Pandang: SIL/UNHAS. [read inside the full-volume PDF, 144 pp, text layer]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical/sociolinguistic survey; wordlists not printed. p.84 'Dakka has been found to be a separate language'; p.87 Dakka's closest relation is Pannei (72-77%) but it is excluded from the PUS Subfamily; p.91 'No studies have as yet been undertaken in the Dakka, Pannei, and Ulumandak languages.'

sources.citation: Strømme, Kåre J. 1987. UNHAS-SIL sociolinguistic survey: Kabupaten Polewali Mamasa, west-central section [PUS2]. Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 5: 17-40.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; survey of the Pitu Ulunna Salu dialect chain in the Mambi highlands; Dakka not covered.

sources.citation: Stokhof, W. A. L. (ed.), with Alma E. Almanar. 1984. Holle lists: vocabularies in languages of Indonesia, vol. 7/3: Central Sulawesi, South-West Sulawesi. (Materials in Languages of Indonesia 26.) Pacific Linguistics D-62. Canberra: ANU. iv+255 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: nothing: list 121 has no notes section; no accent marks; the note 'The stress is on the penultimate syllable, as in Malay' on p.37 belongs to list 192 (Salumpang/Makale = Sa'dan Toraja), not to this list

sources.citation: Veen, H. van der. 1929. Nota betreffende de grenzen van de Sa'dansche taalgroep en het haar aanverwante taalgebied. Tijdschrift voor Indische Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde (TBG) 69: 58-96. Batavia: Albrecht & Co.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Dialect-geographic note on sound correspondences (w>h, r>ch, loss of final l/r/s, vowel qualities a>o 'Dakka (Tapango) kepi', pepet reflexes, palatals), pronouns and negators across the P.Oe.S. area vs Sa'dan and Mandar; no mention of klemtoon/accent anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent klemtoon/klem/accent/nadruk/toon over pp.58-96: 0 hits). First-hand Dakka lexical forms only.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only Indonesian academic article found that concerns the Dakka community; ethnography of communication, very unlikely to state stress but might cite an unpublished local skripsi on bahasa Dakka.

sources.note: Nothing; Dakka is listed only as one of the areas where 'bahasa Mamasa' is spoken; no separate Dakka entry, no phonology.

sources.note: Government dialect-mapping reports sometimes include a short 'fonologi' note per observation point; the only Indonesian-language channel likely to hold any Dakka phonological remarks.

sources.note: Only other linguistic work on the Pitu Ulunna Salu complex; built on ~18 SIL survey wordlists in phonetic transcription and may include the 1983-86 Dakka (Palitakan) list with stress marks or a remark on accent placement across the group. Would be the only chance of a first-hand Dakka datum short of new fieldwork.

sources.citation: SIL Indonesia / UNHAS-SIL survey archive: Dakka (Palitakan village) 1983-1986 survey wordlist (Sulawesi umbrella wordlist, phonetic transcription), underlying Strømme & Valkama 1987; SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 37718 and unpublished wordlist holdings.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The transcribed wordlist is the only primary Dakka data known to exist; SIL Sulawesi survey lists normally mark stress, which would show whether Dakka patterns with penultimate-stress PUS/Mandar neighbours.
